findings.location: Paragraph about tractors (source.html third paragraph starting "Forty-plus years ago...")
findings.source_quote: This causes most farmers to rely on the expertise of specialized repairmen which also cost a lot of money.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate or replace the English loanword with a natural Portuguese equivalent. For example: "Isso faz com que a maioria dos agricultores dependa da especialização de reparadores especializados, o que também custa muito dinheiro." or "...dependa da competência de reparadores especializados..."
findings.translation_quote: Isso faz com que a maioria dos agricultores dependa da expertise de reparadores especializados, o que também custa muito dinheiro.

findings.location: Paragraph about the Amish (source.html paragraph beginning "Then there is the issue of cell phones and E-bikes.")
findings.source_quote: From my vantage point observing the Amish of Holmes County, these two items...
findings.suggested_fix: Capitalize the ethnonym to follow Portuguese conventions for proper names: "Amish" should be capitalized. For example: "...observando os Amish do Condado de Holmes, esses dois itens..."
findings.translation_quote: Do meu ponto de observação dos amish do Condado de Holmes, esses dois itens fizeram...

findings.location: Paragraph on losing "saltiness" (source.html paragraph beginning "Then there was Covid.")
findings.source_quote: Let’s check our own interactions to ensure that we are still being God’s “light” and “salt” to this dark world, and that we are not losing our “saltiness”.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider a more idiomatic Portuguese rendering for "saltiness" to improve clarity. For example: "...e que não estamos perdendo a nossa 'salgadura' (ou simplesmente 'o nosso sal')." Either keep "salgadura" and add note/alternative, or use "o nosso sal" for smoother idiom.
findings.translation_quote: ...e que não estamos perdendo nossa “salgadura”. Além disso, há sinais de procura de empregados por toda parte.
